problem: Full finite widening and extreme RN32 cells may dominate FP proof/integration size even though public inference data rarely needs those fast paths. Goal is a correct total kernel and any board, not maximal fast-path coverage.

runtime_option.operand_guard: Accept only exponent1..254 or signedzero(exp0,frac0). Nonzero subnormal/nonfinite must actually clear prepared.valid and go to known-correct exact fallback.
runtime_option.proposal_guard: Require2<=exp32(q)<=253 and fraction(q)!=0 before accepting certificate. All excluded guesses go to exact fallback. This eliminates min-normal, max-finite and exact-power midpoint cases from the fast soundness theorem.
runtime_option.all_input_contract: All original arrays/shapes/NaNs/infinities/subnormals/zeros remain in the actual kernel domain through exact fallback. No new global hNormal assumption in Submission.correct; derive subset premises from runtime guard.
runtime_option.do_not_mutate_frozen: Create a separate source/version only if selected. Current FP-only7cc98e2b and known exact recipes stay unchanged.

proof_leverage.scope: Exact normal and signedzero roots only; can be reused after actual guard and implementation-equivalence link, not inherited by the old total-finite recipe
proof_leverage.uniform_cell: For nonpower fraction and interior exponents, both midpoint raw64 fields remain in a simple uniform bin and upper cell stays below maxFinite32; no abs(S)<=maxFinite shortcut on an unrestricted maxFinite cell.
